item1.justification: The trace misapplies §102 by treating combinations, implied possibilities, and “obvious modifications” as anticipation—especially for claims 17, 29, and 30—and also conflates §112(a) written description with §112(b) indefiniteness.

item2.justification: The conclusions generally identify particular claim limitations and link them to US-2012220818-A1, US-2013303835-A1, or specified terminology in the claims and specification.

item3.justification: The stages materially conflict because claim 17 shifts among single-reference anticipation by different references and combination-based obviousness, while claims 28 and 30 receive inconsistent treatment of the same allegedly novel pull-stimulation limitation.

item4.justification: The examiner’s high strictness is reflected in resolving uncertain disclosures and broad equivalences toward rejection while allowing claim 28 only after expressly finding both novelty and non-obviousness.

item5.justification: The final outcome substantially follows the novelty, obviousness, and §112 analyses by rejecting claims 1–27 and 29–30 while granting claim 28, with claim-specific rationales provided.
